Thanks, Sonia — appreciate the quick turnaround and the files. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before I kick this to AP: 

1) Remit field length: our payments system (batch uploader) will accept a single 70-character "payment reference" field or an extended "remittance note" up to 240 chars. Can you confirm whether the condensed token in the CSV (the short token format) is intended as the authoritative reference, or should we use the full narrative?

2) Currency: PO 8427 is in USD, but our system requires confirmation that the beneficiary prefers USD credited (not receiving-bank conversion). Confirming helps avoid FX mishaps.

3) Bank files: for faster processing, does Evergreen accept an AP ACH file using NACHA standard? If not, we can send a remittance email and upload.

If you prefer, I can loop in our AP specialist (Aditya Rao) to align the upload format and sample mapping.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Hi Jonas (and team),

Answers below — copied AP for completeness: 

1) Use the condensed token as the primary payment reference when your uploader only supports a single short field. The token format in remit_field_mapping.csv maps as: EVG|PO8427|INV2109 (example). If your system supports the longer remittance_note we prefer the full narrative: "PO 8427 | Invoice 2109 | Redwood CustomerRef: PROD-API-452".

2) Currency: Evergreen requests USD crediting to our USD account — please indicate USD on the payment instruction.

3) NACHA/ACH: Yes, we accept NACHA-originated ACH batches. Our bank requires standard CCD+ with the remittance token in the Entry Description when possible; otherwise please include the CSV remittance file in the payment transaction or in the remittance email to ap@evergreentech.com.

We attached the bank details (Evergreen_BankDetails.pdf) and a clean copy of our W-9 (Evergreen_W9.pdf). The CSV includes two example mappings: one for the long narrative (remittance_note) and one for the condensed token (payment_reference).

If AP wants a sample NACHA CCD+ file, we can accept a test ACH micro-deposit verification first (we'll confirm once we see the test credits).

Thanks,
Sonia
